description: Runnable conformance vectors: inputs are shipped inline (base64), so they can be executed without reproducing any firmware build. Covers paths the OVMF reference cannot reach (PE32, HIGHLOW, non-zero TimeDateStamp/CheckSum, the emit-no-value cases) PLUS a representative subset of real rebased modules from that reference. Expected values are produced by producers/reconcile/profile_ref.py, an implementation written from the profile document alone -- NOT by the implementation under test.

vectors.rationale: PE32 (magic 0x10B) with HIGHLOW fixups. NEITHER is present anywhere in the OVMF reference, so this is the only thing testing the 32-bit ImageBase offset (oh+28, 4 bytes) and the 32-bit subtract.
PE32+ with DIR64 fixups -- the path the real image does exercise, kept so the two widths can be compared side by side.
PE32 already at ImageBase 0: nothing to reverse, header normalization alone.
Non-zero ImageBase with NO relocation directory. Profile s4.1 says header normalization alone canonicalizes it.
Non-zero TimeDateStamp and CheckSum. Every real module has these already zeroed by GenFw, so the reference cannot tell whether an implementation zeroes them.

Rebased PE32+ whose image ends AFTER the optional header's first 68 bytes (so s4.2 passes) but BEFORE data-directory index 5. s4.1: an unreadable directory with B != 0 is a failure, not an absence. The reference itself emitted a value here until review.
Relocation block whose BlockSize is odd. Entries are u16, so the last one straddles the block end. s4.1: fail. Unspecified until review; the reference emitted a value.
HIGH(1) fixup. Profile s4.1: any type other than 0/3/10 MUST emit no value rather than a partially-normalized image.

Rebased PE32+ whose .text SizeOfRawData stops before its second fixup target, putting that target in the section's virtual-only tail -- present once loaded, absent from the file. s4.1 maps an RVA only within SizeOfRawData. Earlier revisions specified max(VirtualSize, SizeOfRawData) and mapped the target onto the NEXT section's bytes, emitting a confident wrong value; all three implementations shared the fault.
vectors.reason: rva 0x1008 maps to no section with raw data

vectors.rationale: Rebased PE32+ whose target section has PointerToRawData = 0: it occupies memory but has no bytes in the file. s4.1 requires PointerToRawData != 0 and SizeOfRawData != 0. The widened rule mapped the fixup into the PE header itself.
vectors.reason: rva 0x1000 maps to no section with raw data

vectors.rationale: Rebased PE32+ with .text moved so its fixup targets match no section. s4.1: an RVA matching no section is a failure. Some PE parsers instead fall back to treating the RVA itself as a file offset; the profile does not.
vectors.reason: rva 0x1000 maps to no section with raw data

vectors.rationale: Rebased PE32+ with no relocation directory and IMAGE_FILE_RELOCS_STRIPPED set: the fixups were applied and the table then discarded, so the placement cannot be reversed. Distinct from a module that genuinely has no relocations (flag clear), which still normalizes -- see pe32plus-no-reloc-table-rebased.
vectors.reason: relocations stripped with ImageBase != 0; not reversible

real_module_note: The real modules are edk2 build outputs, licensed BSD-2-Clause-Patent (see the SBOM's declared licence for the subject firmware). Three are shipped rather than all eleven rebased ones: enough to exercise a real PE with a real section layout and thousands of fixups, without adding 6 MB of binaries to a text repository. The full 122-module digest list is in normalized-module-hash-vectors.json.
